contradictions.fact: Season window (Jul-Aug) vs. wider optimal/best-season claims

claims.says: Jul–Aug (inferred from the dates of all documented ascents: Aug 19 2006, Jul 9 2023, Aug 30 2018 x2)
Late July through September, with August as the core optimal month
August into early September is most reliable...
A narrow window in early-to-mid September is possible before fall snow returns...

contradictions.why: season claims the route is only ever done Jul-Aug, but seasonal_guidance, best_season and climate.fall all treat September as a normal/good part of the window, not just a documented gap.
contradictions.internal_resolution: seasonal_guidance/best_season/climate agree with each other on a Jul(late)-Sep window; season is the outlier, apparently confusing 'dates people happened to climb it' with 'the viable season'.

contradictions.fact: Route aspect vs. the ridge/face it actually climbs

claims.says: S
North Ridge
Significant exposure at the north-ridge crux (7,300-7,400 ft) with an airy notch downclimb
climbs a steep brushy slope to gain the peak's long north ridge near 7,300–7,400 ft
North-facing terrain below the crux holds snow later into summer than typical south-facing Cascades approaches.

contradictions.why: aspect says the route/face is south-facing, but face and every piece of route prose (beta, hazards, approach, descent_text, climate) describe it as climbing and crossing north-facing terrain (the 'north ridge crux', 'north face'). A climber checking ASPECT & SUN on Plan would get the wrong sun/snow expectation.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The overwhelming weight of prose (face + beta + hazards + approach + descent_text + climate) says north-facing; aspect='S' looks like the wrong value.

contradictions.fact: Crux/route grade (Class 4, 5.0) vs. the pitch-by-pitch breakdown's max grade (Class 3)

claims.says: Class 4 (5.0 crux)
Exposed Class 4/5.0 notch with krummholz for holds...
5 rows, max difficulty listed is 'Class 3' (Summit gully / North ridge traverse / Brushy slope)

contradictions.why: The route's overall grade and its own crux waypoint both say the hardest move is Class 4/5.0, but the ROUTE BREAKDOWN (pitch_detail) never lists a pitch above Class 3 - the crux notch isn't represented as a row at all.
contradictions.internal_resolution: grade + the crux waypoint agree (Class 4/5.0); pitch_detail is simply missing that segment rather than contradicting the harder grade, but as rendered side by side it reads as a mismatch.

contradictions.fact: Bear canister requirement

claims.says: Bear canister (recommended/required for NPS backcountry camping)
Bear canisters are not required at these particular camps but food must be stored in the lockers or hung
Bear canisters are not on the required list for this camp, but food must be hung or stored properly
Bear canisters not specifically required at this camp; store food properly regardless.

contradictions.why: The gear list tells a climber a canister is 'recommended/required,' but every camp actually used on this route's own itinerary (Purple Point/Harlequin, Fivemile, Swamp Creek) explicitly says canisters are NOT required there.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The three bivy entries are specific and unanimous; the generic gear-list line is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Whether a permit office exists at Stehekin

claims.says: NPS Golden West Visitor Center / Stehekin Ranger Station (Stehekin) for the park/NRA portion...
THERE IS NO PERMIT OFFICE IN STEHEKIN — a walk-up permit has to be collected in person elsewhere in the park complex before you get on the boat

contradictions.why: emergency names a ranger station/visitor center located in Stehekin as the local park contact, while the bivy section explicitly and emphatically denies any permit office exists in Stehekin, which could send a climber there expecting to get a walk-up permit.

contradictions.fact: Route scope: this route's own trip plan/hazards describe summiting a different peak (Bonanza Peak) than its own waypoints reach

claims.says: only two points: 'High Bridge (Stehekin Valley Road)' (Trailhead) and 'Needle Peak Summit' 7,896 ft (Summit) - i.e. the route as plotted ends on Needle Peak
a two-day, multi-summit traverse (Needle Peak → Anonymity Towers → Dark Peak → Bonanza Peak) that produced the first ascent of Bonanza Peak's Northwest Ridge
Day 2: continue the connecting ridge crest to Bonanza Peak's west summit and then the main summit, descending via the Mary Greene Glacier.
The full traverse from Needle Peak to Bonanza Peak crosses two glaciers and multiple rock towers requiring rappels to bypass

contradictions.why: A climber opening this 'Needle Peak / North Ridge' route page and reading the Trip Plan (itinerary) would be planning to climb a totally different, much bigger peak (Bonanza) two days and two glaciers away, while the route's own waypoints (used for the map/summit card) stop at Needle Peak's own summit with no data at all for the rest of the traverse.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route id/name/area filing (Needle Peak) and its waypoints agree the documented endpoint is Needle Peak's summit; overview/beta/itinerary/hazards describe a much longer historical link-up that continues past Needle Peak to Bonanza Peak. It reads as beta for the wrong/bigger objective attached to a Needle Peak route record.

contradictions.fact: Round-trip distance (dist_km vs. stated mileage)

claims.says: a 7-mile, 2,100-foot scramble
Summer: ...roughly 4 to 7 miles round trip...Winter: ...about 5.2 to 8 miles

contradictions.why: dist_km implies a ~2-mile trip while beta and itinerary both describe a 4-8 mile round trip; even read as a one-way figure (doubling to ~4mi) it sits at the extreme low end of the stated range.
contradictions.internal_resolution: dist_km is plausibly a one-way figure (doubling to ~4mi, the low end of the '4 to 7 miles' range), which is the project's known dist_km convention ambiguity rather than a hard error - kept low priority per that caveat.

contradictions.fact: Waypoint list includes a landmark from a different trail/approach

claims.says: 'Lichtenberg Boulders (granitic boulder field on the north side)', distMi 2.5, elev 4683
never mention the Lichtenberg Boulders at all - the described path is Smith Brook Road → fishing trail → Lichtenwasser Lake → saddle → ridge
'Lichtenberg Boulders (granitic boulder field off the Valhalla trail)' - i.e. on the separate Lake Valhalla/Smithbrook Trail approach used by a different route

contradictions.why: This route's own narrative never goes near the boulder field (it heads to Lichtenwasser Lake via the fishing trail, not toward Lake Valhalla), yet its waypoint list stops there anyway - the waypoint appears to be copied in from the sibling route that actually passes it.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Beta/approach/descent_text are specific and self-consistent about the Lichtenwasser Lake line; the Boulders waypoint (only explained as being 'off the Valhalla trail' in the sibling route) looks like contamination from that other route's waypoint list.

routes.name: West Face - West Rib (Lichtenhorn / West Peak)

contradictions.fact: high_point_ft claims the true 5,844 ft summit, but the route's own prose says it tops out lower

claims.says: 'Lichtenberg Mountain main summit (5,844 ft; the route tops out on the west peak at ~5,800 ft)'

The 5,800-foot west peak (The Lichtenhorn) is not the mountain's true summit — the 5,844-foot main summit is a separate, easier top to the east. If you want both, traverse east along the connecting ridge after topping out on the spire.

contradictions.why: TECHNICAL STATS would show a high point of 5,844 ft (the true summit), but the route's own waypoint note and pro_tips both say the standard line only reaches ~5,800 ft on a separate sub-summit, with the true summit requiring an extra optional traverse.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own prose (waypoint note + pro_tips) is explicit and specific that the standard line stops at ~5,800 ft; high_point_ft=5844 overstates what the described route actually reaches.

contradictions.fact: Round-trip distance: three disagreeing figures for the same route

claims.says: 5.6 (≈3.48 mi one-way; doubles to ~7 mi)
3.5 (one-way, i.e. ~7 mi round trip)
Total gain from the trailhead is roughly 2,000-2,500 ft over about 7 miles round trip
A roughly 9-mile round trip, off-trail scramble up Lichtenberg Mountain's southeast slopes
9.2 / '~9 miles round trip'

contradictions.why: Dist header/TECHNICAL STATS could read anywhere from ~2mi (dist_km misread as RT) to ~7mi to ~9mi depending which field is shown, a >25% spread between the two internally-agreeing camps (waypoints+approach ≈7mi vs overview+itinerary ≈9mi).
contradictions.internal_resolution: dist_km (one-way, doubled) and the waypoints' own cumulative mileage agree with the approach paragraph at ~7 mi round trip; overview and the itinerary object's 9/9.2 mi figures are the outlier pair.

contradictions.fact: rope_note quotes a different route's mileage/gain figures

claims.says: No rope needed; Class 2 non-exposed scramble, 7mi/2100ft gain.
'roughly 9-mile round trip...gaining about 2,500 ft' / '~9 miles round trip with about 2,500 ft of gain'

contradictions.why: rope_note's '2100ft' gain figure exactly matches the SIBLING route on this same peak (Southeast Ridge from Lichtenwasser Lake, gain_ft=2100, beta calls it 'a 7-mile, 2,100-foot scramble'), not this route's own stated 2,500 ft / ~9 mi.
contradictions.internal_resolution: This route's own gain_ft and itinerary both say 2,500 ft; rope_note's '2100ft' looks copied from the sibling Lichtenwasser Lake route rather than describing this line.

contradictions.fact: gain_ft/loss_ft asymmetry for an out-and-back reversal

claims.says: Descend by the same line used on the ascent... reverse the traverse...

contradictions.why: The route is described as reversing the exact ascent line (an out-and-back), so gain and loss should match; the top-level loss_ft (2100) disagrees with the route's own itinerary object (2500/2500) by 400 ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary.gainFt=lossFt=2500 is internally symmetric and matches gain_ft; top-level loss_ft=2100 is the outlier.

Jul-Oct
status 'marginal', early snow possible

contradictions.fact: Avalanche hazard: 'N/A' vs. a listed cornice/avalanche hazard on the same Safety tab

claims.says: N/A - non-glaciated summer/fall scramble route...not this Jul-Oct SE route
cornices/avalanche terrain if attempted with snow cover

contradictions.why: The AVALANCHE box says N/A right next to a KNOWN HAZARDS bullet that names avalanche/cornice terrain; the obj_haz wording is conditional ('if attempted with snow cover') so this mostly reconciles, but the juxtaposition could still read as contradictory.
contradictions.internal_resolution: obj_haz's hazard is explicitly conditional on an off-season snow attempt, consistent with avalanche.zone's N/A for the normal Jul-Oct dry-season climb.

contradictions.fact: Total elevation gain: 2,100 ft (header) vs. 1,800 ft (beta and itinerary)

claims.says: roughly 1,800 ft of elevation gain
about 7-7.5 miles round trip and 1,800 ft gain

contradictions.why: The header GAIN stat (2,100 ft) is ~17% higher than every other statement of this route's gain (beta and both itinerary fields all say 1,800 ft).
contradictions.internal_resolution: Trailhead elevation (4,000 ft) to summit (5,747 ft) is 1,747 ft, matching the 1,800 ft figure used consistently in beta and itinerary; gain_ft=2100/loss_ft=2100 are the outliers.

contradictions.fact: Round-trip distance: three disagreeing figures

claims.says: about 6.4 miles round trip
7.5 / 'about 7-7.5 miles round trip'
3.5 (one-way, i.e. ~7mi RT)
roughly 8-9 miles round trip

contradictions.why: Beta's 6.4mi, the itinerary/waypoints' ~7-7.5mi, and partner_requirements' 8-9mi are three different round-trip mileages for the same hike, a >30% spread top to bottom.

contradictions.fact: Road/trailhead access: current closure vs. normal driving directions given elsewhere

claims.says: Closed to vehicles indefinitely (storm damage) as of mid-2026 — no reopening estimate as of the last USFS update; confirm current status before driving.
FR 6700 has been closed to vehicles since a Forest Service order (effective May 20, 2026)...

From US Highway 2 about 4 miles east of Stevens Pass, turn onto Smith Brook Road (Forest Road 6700) and follow the gravel road roughly 2.6-2.8 miles to the Smithbrook Trailhead (el. ~4,000 ft; no fee, no Northwest Forest Pass required).
Take US 2 to a point about 4 miles east of Stevens Pass and turn onto Smith Brook Road, Forest Road 6700. Follow the gravel road roughly 2.6 to 2.8 miles to the Smithbrook Trailhead...

contradictions.why: GETTING THERE (road) tells a climber the access road is currently closed indefinitely by storm damage, while the APPROACH prose and the trailhead waypoint's own directions both describe simply driving straight up it with no caveat - a party following the approach text would not know the drive is currently impossible.
contradictions.internal_resolution: road.status/driveNote are the most specific and dated claim (a named 2026 closure order); approach/waypoints simply weren't updated to reflect it.

contradictions.fact: Round-trip distance (dist_km vs. waypoints/itinerary)

claims.says: 2.7 (one-way)
5.4 / 'about 5.4 miles round trip'

contradictions.why: dist_km implies roughly a 1-mile trip (whether read as one-way or round trip), while the route's own waypoint list (2.7mi one-way) and itinerary (5.4mi round trip) agree closely with each other at over 5x that distance.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Waypoints and itinerary agree at ~5.4mi RT; dist_km=1.6 is the outlier and too small even doubled.

contradictions.fact: Total gain stated as 2,400 ft in one place, 1,696 ft everywhere else

claims.says: roughly 6-7 hours car-to-car for 2,400 ft of gain and about 5.4 miles round trip

contradictions.why: itinerary.totalNote states 2,400 ft of gain, a ~700 ft (41%) jump over the same itinerary object's own day entry and the top-level gain_ft, both of which say 1,696 ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Trailhead (4,000 ft) to summit (5,696 ft) is exactly 1,696 ft, matching gain_ft and itinerary.days[0].gainFt; totalNote's '2,400 ft' is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Descent direction: which face/gully the first rappel(s) drop onto

claims.says: 2 rappels down slabs north of the exit gully (one party used two 30m ropes), plus a protected wet-ledge traverse
Two rappels down slabs north of the exit gully, a protected traverse across a wet ledge to the east gully, then a long glissade down the Colchuck Glacier...
From the summit, descend back to the upper rock band; the single rappel from there drops onto the ledge on the southeast face.
First of the rappels down the gully lying east of the top of the Northeast Couloir, entered from the southeast-face ledge.

contradictions.why: The prose summary (rappels/descent/descent_text) says the rappels go down slabs NORTH of the exit gully before reaching the east gully; the RAPPELS table (rappel_detail) instead has the first rappel landing on a ledge on the SOUTHEAST face before reaching the (east) gully - a real disagreement about which direction off the summit a party first descends, on a route with no fixed anchors.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The two accounts partly reconcile (both end up traversing to an 'east' gully toward the Colchuck Glacier), but disagree specifically on the compass direction/face of the first rappel(s) (north-of-gully slabs vs. southeast face).

contradictions.fact: Access/closure info names the wrong trailhead system (Teanaway/Ingalls Creek instead of this route's own Stuart Lake/Icicle Creek approach)

claims.says: Stuart Lake Trailhead (end of Icicle Creek Road/FR-7600-7601 near Leavenworth)
Wenatchee River Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Leavenworth)
Northwest Forest Pass ($5/day or $30/annual) at the Teanaway/Ingalls Creek trailheads.
Beverly Creek/Fourth Creek Pass...and several nearby Teanaway trails...were closed...confirm current status with the Cle Elum Ranger District before planning a Teanaway-side approach.

contradictions.why: This route's own approach/road/waypoints are unanimous that it starts from the Stuart Lake Trailhead off Icicle Creek Road (Wenatchee River Ranger District), but access.parking_pass and access.closures instead discuss the Teanaway/Ingalls Creek trailheads and the Cle Elum Ranger District - a different approach system entirely (used by Argonaut's south-side routes, per this route's own bivy notes, which explicitly say the north-side basin camp 'serves only Argonaut's north side'). A climber reading GETTING THERE/ACCESS would get pass and closure info for the wrong road.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach/road/waypoints/approach_logistics/emergency.rangerStation are all specific and consistent about Icicle Creek/Stuart Lake; access.parking_pass and access.closures look copied from a Teanaway-side (Ingalls/south-side) route.

contradictions.fact: Day-2 elapsed time in the schedule (14.5 hrs) vs. the day's stated hours (11)

claims.says: 4:00 AM Leave camp ... 6:30 PM Reach trailhead

contradictions.why: The schedule's own first and last entries for day 2 span 4:00 AM to 6:30 PM, 14.5 hours, 3.5 hours more than the day's stated 'hours: 11' - a meaningful gap for a route whose own turnaround guidance stresses a firm early-afternoon cutoff.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The schedule entries are specific clock times; 'hours: 11' appears to undercount the day by roughly 3.5 hours.

contradictions.fact: Pitch count: 7 vs. '6-8'

claims.says: 7 / 'climbing roughly seven pitches of class 4 to 5.6 granite'
7 numbered rows (pitch 1-7)
The route is described as 6-8 pitches of Class 4 to 5.6
the arete gives six to eight pitches of blocky, generally solid Class 4 to 5.6

contradictions.why: The top-level pitches field, overview, and the numbered ROUTE BREAKDOWN all agree on 7 pitches, but detailed_rack and the approach_variant text both hedge to '6-8,' which could read as a different pitch count for the same climb.
contradictions.internal_resolution: pitches=7 and the 7 numbered pitch_detail rows are the specific, internally-consistent count; the '6-8' phrasing elsewhere is imprecise hedging rather than a real conflicting count.
